Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 21.07.2014 passed by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT-V, Chitradurga, in MVC No.377/2013, seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Medical expenses Rs.1,35,300/-
It is stated that the deceased was doing tailoring and beautician work but there is no evidence to prove income of the deceased.
The accident was occurred on 22.03.2013.

Therefore, the notional income of Rs.8,000/-
is taken into consideration as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As the deceased was aged NC: 2024:KHC:51078 about 30 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.

Further, as per principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the monthly income of the deceased is to be added towards 'Loss of Future Prospects in Life', i.e., Rs.3,200/- (Rs.8,000/- x 40%).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at Rs.11,200/- (Rs.8,000/- +
Rs.3,200/-).
There are three legal heirs.
Hence, 1/3rd of the amount would be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and the remaining 2/3rd would be the contribution for the family.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss of Dependency' is hereby recalculated and quantified as follows:
Rs.8,000 + 3,200 (40% of 8000) x 2/3 x 17 x 12 = Rs.15,23,200/-
NC: 2024:KHC:51078 6.
The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 'loss of consortium of petitioner No.1' which is on the lesser side.

As per Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, Rs.40,000/-
is to be awarded under the head 'loss of consortium'.

reported in AIR 2022 SC 85, for every three years 10% income is to be raised.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable to reduce the same to a sum of Rs.16,500/- under the head 'transportation of dead NC: 2024:KHC:51078 body,

Further, the Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head 'loss of estate'.

. Particulars Compensation awarded (in Rs.)
1. Loss of dependency Rs.15,23,200.00 2. Loss of consortium Rs.1,32,000.00 3. Loss of estate Rs.16,500.00 4. Transportation of dead body, Rs.16,500.00 funeral expenses, etc.
5.
Medical expenses Rs.1,35,300.00 TOTAL Rs.18,23,500.00 9.
The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.15,07,800/-, but the appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.18,23,500/- as against Rs.15,07,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum which is on the higher side and hence, this Court deems just and NC: 2024:KHC:51078 proper to grant 6% interest per annum.
Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.18,23,500/- along with interest at 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of realization.

10. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.377/2013 dated 21.07.2014 by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT-V, Chitradurga is hereby modified holding that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,23,500/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
iii. The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
iv. Costs made easy.
v. Draw award accordingly.

SD/-
